label: Hull shift report
info: Writes the three shift report tables of site Hull from the Insights Hub API (phase 1: the report lines). Read calls only. Needs the Config tab.

name: [1] TRIGGERS & SITE SETTINGS
info: STAGE 1 - TRIGGERS AND SITE SETTINGS. Site Hull. Writes the three SHIFT REPORT tables from the Insights Hub API, one file per table and production day: rpt_window (asset x window: the day and each shift run), rpt_hour (asset x hour) and rpt_event (one row per stop). Phase 1: the report lines of the Config tab (reportLineIds), no machines yet. The production day starts at dayStartLocal o'clock local time (Config, time zone Europe/London), so it is 23, 24 or 25 hours long. Schedule: daily, builds the days that ended at least two hours before (REBUILD_DAYS in 1.1). Backfill: edit the inject payload {"start":"YYYY-MM-DD","end":"YYYY-MM-DD"} (production days) and click the button. Both go through 1.1 SITE SETTINGS, the only node of this flow to edit: site name, dry-run switch, rebuild days, folder names. The shared settings (credentials, root folder, platform, planned reason roots, the lines, day start and time zone of the site) come from the Config tab through global context. dryRun is true by default: set it to false to write files. 1.2 sends ONE MESSAGE PER DAY with its exact window (dayFromMs, dayToMs); the delay node starts one day every 5 s.

name: [2] DAY SETUP
info: STAGE 2 - one message per day: token request, OEE asset list (2.3 keeps a short copy of it), choose the report lines of the Config tab, one message per line (one per second). 2.5 asks Asset Management for the machines below the line, 2.6 packs the answer with its line, a join waits for the lists of all lines and 2.7 sends one message per asset: every line and every child that is a configured OEE asset and is not in reportExcludeNames of the Config tab (machines come in by themselves). The messages of the day form one group (msg.parts), so the join of stage 10 waits for all of them without keeping any rows in the flow context (the context accepts 2 MB per value only). Function nodes cannot use fetch in the VFC, so every call is an http request node: the function before it sets msg.method, msg.url and msg.headers. A failure goes to the LOG and nothing is written for that day.

name: [3] ASSET KPIs
info: STAGE 3 - one asset. 3.1 and 3.2: Asset Management GET asset (hierarchyPath), then evaluateKPIs POST over the exact window of the day (read-style, groupedByDateTime=true, recursive=false, no ORDER filter). 3.3 checks the response, 3.4 pivots it to one entry per hour. Every asset ends at the join, also when skipped or failed (link "to JOIN"), so the join never waits for a missing message.

name: [4] ASSET SHIFTS
info: STAGE 4 - one asset. The shift of an hour comes from the calendar of the asset. 4.1 asks the OEE config for the calendar id and the product collection id, 4.2 asks the calendar events that cover the production day, 4.3 turns them into shift rules (freq, interval, start, until, duration). A failed call or an asset without a calendar fails the day (link "to JOIN").

name: [5] ASSET PRODUCTS
info: STAGE 5 - one asset. 5.1 asks filterValues for the products and orders of the production day (the lists behind the Product and Order dropdowns of the OEE app). 5.2 checks the answer and asks the product list (name, code, description, design speed) of the product collection of the asset. A day without any product or order goes straight to "to ASSIGN"; an asset without a product collection goes on without master data ("to VALUES"). A failed call fails the day (link "to JOIN").

name: [6] VALUE KPIs
info: STAGE 6 - one asset. 6.1 keeps the master data of the products of the day and sends ONE MESSAGE PER PRODUCT AND PER ORDER (one per second). 6.2 builds the evaluateKPIs POST (read-style, hourly) filtered on that product or order. 6.3 keeps the hours that have parts and waits until every value of the asset is in (the state is kept in flow context under valueRuns, so no second split is needed). A failed call fails the day (link "to JOIN").

name: [7] ASSIGN & ROWS
info: STAGE 7 - one asset. 7.1 gives every hour its product and order: the value that has parts in that hour; an hour without parts takes the value of the hour before it (the first hours take the next value). 7.2 adds the shift and the design speed per minute to every hour. 7.3 builds the rpt_hour rows (one per hour, local date and time, minutes, speed, capacity). 7.4 builds the rpt_window rows: the production day and every run of hours in the same shift, from the SUMS of the hourly KPIs; the ratios (availability = net production time / operational time, performance = total / theoretical output, quality = good / total, OEE = the three multiplied) are calculated again from the sums, the same formulas as the OEE app, so no extra API call is needed.

name: [8] ASSET SEGMENTS
info: STAGE 8 - one asset. A line goes straight on ("to STOPS"). A machine: 8.1 asks the time segments of the day (timeModelCategoryDistribution, read-style POST, one answer for the whole day), 8.2 adds the minutes per group to every window row: Run = ran, Unplanned Downtime = faults, Lack of resources = waiting, Planned Downtime = planned, everything else (also a segment without a category) = other. The segments are cut to the window (day and each shift run). operator_min stays empty: Insights Hub has no category for operator stops (the reason of a stop comes from the machine status mapping), so operator stops are counted in the groups above until Reckitt defines a rule. A failed call fails the day (link "to JOIN").

name: [9] ASSET STOPS
info: STAGE 9 - one asset. 9.1 downtimeReasons GET over the exact window of the day (size 5000, one page), 9.2 checks the response, 9.3 builds the rpt_event rows (one per stop that starts inside the production day: UTC and local time, shift, kind microstop, planned or unplanned, reason and reason path, minutes, comment count, product and order of the hour of the stop, loss units = design speed per minute x minutes), 9.4 builds the result of the asset and sends it to the wait node (link "to JOIN").

name: [10] JOIN & BUILD TABLES
info: STAGE 10 - the join waits for all assets of the day (the lines and their machines). 10.1 collects the results, 10.2 decides: it writes NOTHING if any asset failed (no half days) and nothing in dry-run mode, 10.3 builds one message per table. Output 1 of 10.3 = rpt_window, 2 = rpt_hour, 3 = rpt_event, 4 = log.

name: [11] WRITE rpt_window
info: STAGE 11 - parquet node, path and write object for rpt_window (asset x window: the day and each shift run). The path is <root>/shift_report/rpt_window/site=<site>/rpt_window_<production day>.parquet, the same on every rerun, so a rerun replaces the day. Types: UTF8 (STRING), INT64, DOUBLE, TIMESTAMP_MILLIS. Days are text YYYY-MM-DD.

name: [12] WRITE rpt_hour
info: STAGE 12 - parquet node, path and write object for rpt_hour (asset x hour). The path is <root>/shift_report/rpt_hour/site=<site>/rpt_hour_<production day>.parquet, the same on every rerun, so a rerun replaces the day. Types: UTF8 (STRING), INT64, DOUBLE, TIMESTAMP_MILLIS. Days are text YYYY-MM-DD.

name: [13] WRITE rpt_event
info: STAGE 13 - parquet node, path and write object for rpt_event (one row per stop). The path is <root>/shift_report/rpt_event/site=<site>/rpt_event_<production day>.parquet, the same on every rerun, so a rerun replaces the day. Types: UTF8 (STRING), INT64, DOUBLE, TIMESTAMP_MILLIS. Days are text YYYY-MM-DD.

name: [14] ERRORS
info: STAGE 14 - a catch node takes every error raised by a node of this tab and turns it into a log line with the name of the node and the message of the API (for example the limit message of evaluateKPIs). Errors of the log nodes themselves are not logged again.

name: [15] LOG
info: STAGE 15 - every log line arrives here through the link "to LOG". 1 turns a line into a row (time, flow, site, production day, level) and shows it in the debug sidebar. The join collects the rows for 30 s, the delay lets one batch pass every 10 s so two writes do not overlap, 3 sets the file of the month and the read node loads the old file. A read of a file that does not exist answers nothing (only a warning), so the same batch also goes through a 10 s wait to the append step. The log is written whatever the dry-run switch says.

name: [16] LOG WRITE
info: STAGE 16 - adds the rows of the batch to the old file and writes the whole file back (the data lake has no append). Columns: ts_utc, seq, flow, site, production_day, mode, level, source, message. Every field is quoted, line breaks become a space. The batch arrives twice (read answer and the wait) and is written once. If the read gives no answer for a file this flow wrote before, a new file with a time stamp is written, so the history is never replaced.
